title: Power Automate process mining: tabs and customisable layouts in the process intelligence experience
summary: Hold: the proposed API changes ownership of a process-version row, but Microsoft does not establish that it transfers ownership of the process or its tabs. The admin path also includes a step absent from its cited instructions, and the briefing extends process-owner handover guidance to tab ownership without evidence.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default is on, with automatic enablement for admins, makers and marketers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate licence for the process intelligence experience is published, and its three cited feature pages name no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience licensing pricing capacity preview public tabs; process intelligence experience preview license. claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no feature-specific UI or automation switch to disable this experience or restrict tab sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience admin disable enable sharing public tabs settings API; Power Platform API disable; PowerShell CLI disable tabs sharing; Dataverse sharing settings. Read feature pages, security page and Power Apps PowerShell/sharing-limits search excerpts; none names this switch.

claims.claim: The cited sharing page gives Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records.
claims.quote: 1. Sign in to Power Platform admin center. 2. Select the environment where the process is located. 3. On the command bar, select Settings. 4. Under Users + permissions, select Users. 5. Select the leaving user. 6. On the command bar, select Reassign records.
claims.fix: Use the path the cited page actually gives: 'environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records'. Remove the added 'Environments' step from the front matter and rendered table.

claims.claim: PATCH /msdyn_pmprocessversions(msdyn_pmprocessversionid) with ownerid is the automation equivalent of reassigning a departed user's process ownership.
claims.quote: Searched: process mining owner msdyn_pmprocessversion API reassign. Opened the PM Process Version reference and process-mining-share. Assign/PATCH and ownerid exist for version rows; neither page establishes this single-row operation as process-owner reassignment.
claims.fix: Remove the API call from this ownership control and remove the prose calling it a documented process-owner reassignment route. Retain the verified UI procedure; the cited API reference establishes only assignment of PM Process Version rows, not equivalent reassignment of a process and its associated records.

claims.claim: The process intelligence experience is the next-generation process-analysis interface in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Change & support
claims.claim: The experience improves on the previous single fixed process overview with multiple configurable tabs.
claims.quote: Flexibility: Create multiple tabs with different card configurations instead of a single fixed view.

claims.claim: Users can arrange, resize and configure dashboard cards.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.claim: Each process view can have its own set of analytical tabs.
claims.quote: You can have an independent set of analytical tabs per view.

claims.claim: Process views can be defined in the Process Mining desktop application.
claims.quote: Process views can be defined in the Process Mining desktop application.

claims.claim: The (+) button creates a tab through the Add tab dialog.
claims.quote: At the end of the tab bar, select (+). The Add tab dialog opens.

claims.claim: The Edit tabs menu also offers tab creation.
claims.quote: The Edit tabs context menu displays: ... Add tab button: + Add tab option at the bottom.

claims.claim: Tabs can be renamed.
claims.quote: Rename tab: Change the tab's name.

claims.claim: Tabs can be duplicated.
claims.quote: Duplicate tab: Create a copy of the tab with all its cards and layout.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Tabs can be deleted.
claims.quote: Delete tab: Remove the tab from the dashboard.

claims.claim: Tabs can be moved to change their order.
claims.quote: Move up: Shift the tab one position to the left in the tab bar. Move down: Shift the tab one position to the right in the tab bar.

claims.where: What's changing; Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Make public shares an individual tab with other users.
claims.quote: Make public: Share the tab with other users (indicated by person icon with lock).

claims.claim: Edit layout opens a mode with an Add card panel.
claims.quote: To begin to customize your layout, select Edit layout in the top-right corner of the interface. ... The Add card panel becomes accessible.

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers KPI cards.
claims.quote: KPI: Display key performance indicators with large numeric values

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers Donut chart cards.
claims.quote: Donut chart: Show proportional data in a circular, segmented format.

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers Process map cards.
claims.quote: Process map: Visualize the process flow with activities and connections.

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers Vertical bar chart cards.
claims.quote: Vertical bar chart: Compare values across categories using vertical bars.

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers Horizontal bar chart cards.
claims.quote: Horizontal bar chart: Compare values using horizontal bars.

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers Line chart cards.
claims.quote: Line chart: Display trends and changes over time.

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers Statistical grid cards.
claims.quote: Statistical grid: Present detailed data in a tabular format.

claims.claim: The Add card panel offers Variant DNA cards.
claims.quote: Variant DNA: Analyze process variant patterns and characteristics

claims.claim: Cards are arranged on a grid.
claims.quote: The layout system uses a grid-based arrangement, which allows cards to snap to alignment positions as you move them.

claims.claim: Tab filters apply to all cards on the current tab.
claims.quote: Filters apply to all cards and visualizations on the current tab.

claims.claim: Persistent filters are saved with the tab layout.
claims.quote: Add persistent filters: Button to create filters that apply across all cards. They're saved with the tab layout

claims.where: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Persistent filters cannot be removed in viewing mode.
claims.quote: They're saved with the tab layout and can't be removed when viewing the tab.

claims.claim: The tab-management page labels its layout link as preview.
claims.quote: Customize layouts in process intelligence studio (preview)

claims.claim: The documentation does not identify which individual cards or functions remain in preview.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience preview license; licensing pricing capacity preview public tabs. Opened tab management, overview and dynamic layout. The tab page labels the layout link preview; the layout page supplies no per-card release-status breakdown.

claims.claim: Specific tabs or entire dashboard configurations can be shared with team members.
claims.quote: Collaboration: Share specific tabs or entire dashboard configurations with team members.

claims.claim: The feature documentation does not define the audience of a public tab or its interaction with underlying process access.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience public permissions; admin disable enable sharing public tabs settings API. Opened tab management, overview, security and process sharing. Public tabs are described as shared with other users, without specifying the relationship to process permissions.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Process mining access relies on environment security and Dataverse security roles.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: Environment Maker can create, share and contribute to processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.claim: Process Mining User can only view created process reports.
claims.quote: The Process Mining User security role can only view created process reports.

claims.claim: Process Mining Application is an internal role that should not be assigned to users.
claims.quote: The Process Mining Application is an internal security role that process mining uses. ... Don't assign this security role to users.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify Process Mining User or Process Mining Application privileges.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.where: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Conditional Access policies limiting Power Automate must include both Power Apps and Power Automate in Cloud apps.
claims.quote: If you're using Conditional Access polices to limit access to Power Automate and its features, the following apps must be included in Cloud apps policy application: Power Apps; Power Automate

claims.claim: The feature pages describe no new autonomous actions on tenant data.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience autonomous actions data. Opened overview, tab management and dynamic layout. They describe analysis, visualization, filters and dashboard editing, not autonomous execution against tenant business data.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A process co-owner does not automatically become the process owner when the owner's account is disabled.
claims.quote: When a process owner's account is disabled, the co-owner of the process doesn't automatically become a new process owner.

claims.claim: A departing tab owner does not hand tabs over automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: process mining tabs owner leaves. Opened process-mining-share, tab management and experience overview. The handover statement concerns a process owner's disabled account; none describes tab ownership succession.
claims.fix: Replace 'A tab owner who leaves does not hand tabs over automatically' with 'When a process owner's account is disabled, a process co-owner does not automatically become the process owner.' Do not extend process-record reassignment to tab ownership.

claims.claim: No meter or price specific to the process intelligence experience is published.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience licensing pricing capacity preview public tabs; meter price capacity. Opened feature pages and process-advisor-overview; read Power Platform licensing FAQ and pay-as-you-go meters excerpts. No experience-specific price or meter was stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Stored process data mostly consumes Dataverse file capacity.
claims.quote: The process data we store uses mostly file capacity.

claims.claim: Importing large amounts of process data can exhaust Dataverse storage.
claims.quote: Depending on the size of the process data you import, you might run out of Dataverse storage capacity.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe incremental capacity consumption for additional cards and tabs.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience licensing pricing capacity preview public tabs; meter price capacity. Opened overview, tab management, dynamic layout and process-advisor-overview. No per-card or per-tab capacity rule was stated.

claims.claim: Process mining requires a Power Platform environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Power Platform environment with a Microsoft Dataverse database.

claims.claim: Process-mining prerequisites include the licences or trials required for the selected capabilities.
claims.quote: The required licenses or trials depending on the capabilities you want access to.

claims.claim: Administrators and system customizers can access every process created in the environment.
claims.quote: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes created in the environment.

claims.claim: The desktop app is needed to define process views.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience views desktop. Opened experience overview and read desktop process-hub excerpts. Microsoft says views can be defined in the desktop app and a default view is automatic; it does not state the mandatory prerequisite as written.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Process views can be defined in the Process Mining desktop application; a default view is provided automatically after process creation.' This is the wording supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/process-mining-studio-overview.

claims.claim: Some Dataverse privileges are set by default so built-in roles can use process mining without administrator action.
claims.quote: Some privileges are set by default in Dataverse. This allows built-in security roles to use the process mining capability without further actions from system administrators.

claims.claim: The process-sharing page does not specify a named administrator security role required to execute its reassignment procedure.
claims.quote: The administrator should perform the following steps.

claims.claim: The cited sources do not establish that the process owner's identity is stored in the PM Process Version table.
claims.quote: Searched: process mining owner msdyn_pmprocessversion API reassign. Read process-mining-share and the PM Process Version reference, including its ownerid and parent-process relationship excerpts. They do not identify version-row ownership as ownership of the process.

claims.claim: Layout changes can be saved to the tab.
claims.quote: Save changes made in edit layout mode by selecting Save when exiting edit mode.

claims.claim: The feature documentation names no new data source introduced by this interface.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience new data sources; autonomous actions data. Opened overview, tab management and dynamic layout. Their subject is analysis of process data and dashboard configuration, not a new ingestion source.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The checklist refers to a roles control in the table and asks readers to check Conditional Access and capacity, but those controls have no rows.
claims.quote: 'using the roles control in the table'; 'Check that any Conditional Access policy'; 'Watch Dataverse file capacity'. The table contains only an experience/sharing-switch gap and departed-user record ownership.
claims.fix: Remove 'using the roles control in the table'. The role-inventory, Conditional Access and capacity-monitoring checklist steps have no corresponding controls-table rows; do not describe the existing table as providing those controls.

claims.claim: The abbreviated reassignment path is Settings > Users + permissions > Users > Reassign records.
claims.quote: Select the environment where the process is located. ... select Settings. ... select Users. Select the leaving user. On the command bar, select Reassign records.
claims.fix: Give the full cited path: 'Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records'. The omitted environment and user selections are the subject-selection steps.
